title: Dragging a bar's end tracks the pointer without flickering
goal: User 2026-09-26: 'when I drag a rectangle to the video, then try to resize the duration in the track by grabbing the right edge, I move it left and it seems to flicker while dragging left. Like it doesn't want to just track with the mouse. Busted.' The row itself landed in 3235cde1 (anything drawn on a video gets its own row). Reproduce first, frame by frame, then fix. Candidate causes to test, not assume: snapping toggling on and off near the playhead or a clip edge as the pointer moves (see the done task a-trim-handle-catches-on-a-cut-as-it-passes), the drag reading the bar's live frame as its origin so each move feeds back into the next, a clamp against the clip under it fighting the pointer, or the whole timeline re-laying out on every change (ClipBarDrag.swift, TimelineTrackRows.swift). Standard: in Premiere and Final Cut the edge sits under the pointer every frame, snapping only when within a few points and letting go cleanly.
acceptance: Reproduced first: a walk at Next defaults draws a rectangle on a recording, drags its bar's right edge left in 30+ small steps, records the edge's x and the pointer's x at every step, and shows the mismatch or jitter today

Core test (PhotonzCore): an edge drag computed from the drag's START state and the pointer delta, never from the live frame; the out point is monotonic in the pointer and equals it to within one frame except while snapped

Snapping engages within a small fixed distance of the playhead, other edges and keys, holds while inside it, and releases cleanly when leaving, with no alternation between two positions; holding Cmd (or N, as in Premiere) turns snapping off for the drag
The same holds for the left edge, for moving a whole bar, for a clip's trim handles and for a caption word chip
The bar redraws only itself while dragging, at 60fps, with no other row re-laying out; measured in the walk
After the fix the walk shows the edge within one frame of the pointer at every step, and photographs the bar mid-drag

log.note: Reproduced 2026-09-26 with a new walk step, dragGrip (real mouse events posted to the window, grip position read back after each move): bar-end-follows-the-pointer-walk at Next defaults, Rectangle clip end pulled -160pt in 40 moves -> '41 steps, worst 160.0pt off the pointer, went back on itself 19 times'. The trace (grip-trace-17.json) alternated: grip under the pointer on odd moves, back at the grab point on even moves.

Cause: ClipPiecesBar's edge DragGesture read the hand in the grip's own .local space, and the grip is drawn where the drag has it (.offset), so each move of the grip was subtracted from the next reading. Not snapping, not a clamp. Same pattern in the strip's body carry, key diamonds, fade handles, transition band ends (ClipPiecesBar + TimelineLaneDrop) and KeyLanesView key drags; all now read in ClipPiecesBar.handSpace (.global). Trim tool handles and caption word/cue lanes were already in a fixed space. TimelineTrackSelect already carried a comment about exactly this.

Also: an edge held at its start by a magnet it already lines up with (rectangle end = recording end) reported no catch, so no snap line; ClipBarDrag.landing now keeps snappedTo on an unmoved landing (GripTraceTests). Cmd held on an edge drag frees it of every magnet (EditorState.updateClipBarDrag free:), matching Cmd on the canvas and in Trim; S still toggles snapping for the whole timeline. Walk proves it: same drag caught 3 without Cmd, 0 with.

Rebuilds: 40 moves rebuilt every track row (132) and every bar (130) because the ruler and each row's keyed-lanes check read the whole clipBarDrag session. Now EditorState keeps clipBarInHandIDs and clipBarHeldTimelineMS (set only at grab and let go), bars read shownDocument(forClip:), rows are Equatable (.equatable()) and use keyLanesAtRest: 53 row and 52 bar builds (the dragged one per move, the rest at grab and release). Walk claims trackRow atMost 60. Also moved the piece's walk marker before its .offset so a clip not starting at 0 is pressed where it is drawn.

Adversarial review: a Premiere/FCP user expects the edge to stay glued to the pointer, snap within a few points, and let go cleanly; that now holds for right end, left end and body (0.0pt worst, 0 reversals). Mock (video.html .clip) draws no end grips or drag pill; the app's grips and pill predate this task and are unchanged. At 60fps: each move was redrawn within the walk's 30ms read window at every step; no frame timer was run.

left rough (log only): the right hand panel still rebuilds each move of a bar drag (~35 of 40); not a row, not visible as jank in the walk, no task. The older motion strip's timing bars (MotionStripView drag at ~715/842) use .local translation and were not measured; not on the video timeline at Next defaults, so no task until someone sees it. keys-copy-between-layers-walk fails at step 81 exactly as in the 2026-09-25 sweep, already on walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-5.

Shipped in 9d689bd9. Bar ends, whole bars, key diamonds, fade handles and transition band ends read the pointer in a fixed space, so the edge no longer jumps back every other move; Cmd drags an edge free of magnets; only the dragged row and bar rebuild per move (132->53 rows, 130->52 bars over 40 moves). Verified by bar-end-follows-the-pointer-walk at Next defaults (new dragGrip step: 0.0pt worst, 0 reversals for right end, left end and body; was 160pt and 19 reversals), GripTraceTests, full suite 9963 green.
